raw.abstractText: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent the first line of host immune defense against a broad spectrum of microorganisms. Whether naturally occurring or synthetically designed, these small peptides can potently inhibit microbial growth and remain stable under diverse conditions. Most AMPs act by directly disrupting fungal or bacterial membranes. In this study, we identified a glycine-rich peptide with strong antifungal activity against Botrytis cinerea. We further investigated its mode of action (MOA) and demonstrated its preventive antifungal activity in plants. Our work focuses primarily on the in vitro characterization of AMP features in the context of plant-Botrytis interactions.

raw.abstractText: Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) is a powerful reverse genetics tool that enables the transient knockdown of gene expression in plants by exploiting their natural antiviral defense mechanisms. This chapter presents a detailed protocol for applying a Cowpea severe mosaic virus (CPSMV)-based VIGS system to study gene function in soybean (Glycine max), with a focus on symbiotic root nodulation. VIGS allows systemic silencing of target genes, making it especially valuable to study pathways involving systemic signaling. The protocol includes Agrobacterium-mediated propagation of CPSMV variants in Nicotiana benthamiana, followed by mechanical inoculation of soybean plants and nodulation analysis. Detailed steps for vector construction, viral amplification, plant infection, and downstream molecular and phenotypic analyses are provided. This protocol is reproducible, accessible, and suitable for functional genomics studies in soybean, particularly for genes involved in nodulation but also in other developmental or stress-related processes.

raw.abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate metabolic outcomes in women with and without Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS, formerly Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS))) receiving multidisciplinary care through a women's health telehealth platform that combines physician and registered dietitian support.

Methods

Retrospective cohort analysis of 919 women with BMI ≥ 25 initiating care in 2024, with ≥ 6 months follow-up (mean 9.6 months). Participants included 557 with PMOS and 362 without. Outcomes extracted from the electronic health record (EHR) included change in weight, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, fasting insulin, fasting glucose, ALT, AST and total cholesterol between baseline and last measured value. Linear regression models adjusted for baseline values of each outcome, age, BMI, race/ethnicity and follow-up time.

Results

Significant improvements were observed across all metabolic markers for the group overall: HOMA-IR (-14.0%), fasting insulin (-15.6%), fasting glucose (-13.0%), HbA1c (-6.2%), ALT (-21.2%), AST (-25.5%), total cholesterol (-8.0%) and weight (-4.9%). PCOS status was not associated with differential improvement in any outcome after adjustment. GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with greater weight loss; however, improvements were also observed in the no-medication group.

Conclusions

Women with PCOS achieved metabolic improvements equivalent to those without PMOS through a multidisciplinary telehealth model despite presenting with a more adverse metabolic profile at baseline.

raw.abstractText: This study aimed to explore the processing mechanism of single medicinal herbs in compound prescriptions, compare the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic changes of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula before and after processing, and elucidate its underlying mechanism against gastric ulcers. The results showed that six components, namely, corydaline, coptisine chloride, palmatine, berberine chloride, phellopterin, and imperatorin, exerted anti-ulcer activities. The optimal vinegar-processing parameters for Corydalis yanhusuo were determined as follows: processing temperature of 84°C, vinegar dosage of 37%, and baking time of 35 min. Vinegar-processed Corydalis yanhusuo could accelerate the in vivo distribution of alkaloid components in the formula, elevate the plasma concentration, and prolong the in vivo retention time of coumarin components. The synergistic effects of the two types of active ingredients endow the vinegar-processed Yuanhu Zhitong Formula with significantly superior antigastric ulcer activity compared with the raw formula. Moreover, network pharmacology results revealed that this formula exerts therapeutic effects against gastric ulcers mainly by regulating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This study clarified the optimal processing technology and the pharmacodynamic material basis of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula against gastric ulcers, confirmed the efficacy-enhancing effect of processing, and provided data support for the formulation of its processing production standards and clinical medication.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Caffeine is consumed for its presumed cognitive benefits, yet controlled studies have repeatedly failed to find effects on inhibitory control. Cross-sectional work suggests that people with elevated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms may benefit from chronic, moderate caffeine consumption, but whether acute intake improves cognition in proportion to symptom severity has not been tested experimentally.

Aims

We tested whether 250 mg of caffeine improves active inhibition (withholding a prepared response) and reactive inhibition (resolving response conflict), and whether ADHD symptom severity moderates these effects.

Methods

In a preregistered, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, a nonclinical sample of 36 young adults received 250 mg of caffeine or placebo in counterbalanced order, with testing 45 min after ingestion. Active inhibition was assessed with a Go/No-Go task (204 trials), reactive inhibition with an arrow flanker task (200 trials) and symptoms with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale. Mixed-effects models included treatment, symptom severity, their interaction and ten covariates; Bayes factors quantified evidence for the null.

Results

Both tasks produced their benchmark effects (dz = 1.24 and 1.09) and all indices were reliable (split-half r = 0.73-0.98). Caffeine affected neither commission errors (BF01 = 4.98), response criterion (5.14), Go reaction time (2.83), reaction time variability (4.35), flanker reaction time (5.49) nor flanker accuracy (5.09). ADHD symptoms moderated no effect (15 preregistered tests; smallest p = 0.514), yet predicted performance itself (flanker accuracy r = -0.42), indicating that the null is not due to an insensitive measure.

Conclusions

Caffeine produced no acute benefit for either form of inhibition, and ADHD symptoms did not moderate its effects. Bayes factors supported the absence rather than the nondetection of these effects, arguing against an acute improvement of inhibitory control that scales with ADHD symptom severity in nonclinical young adults. Whether this also holds for chronic consumption or for adults with diagnosed ADHD remains to be tested.

raw.abstractText: The collagen triple helix is the most abundant protein structural motif in animals. It tolerates any amino acid in its Xaa and Yaa positions but demands glycine (Gly) at every third position, where the residue packs into the sterically forbidding core of the triple helix and donates the recurring interstrand N-H⋯OC hydrogen bond that stitches the three strands together. (2S)-Proline (Pro) and (2S,4R)-4-hydroxyproline (Hyp) are enriched far above their proteome-wide abundance because they preorganize individual strands into the polyproline II conformation, lowering the entropic cost of folding. We asked whether the triple helix is intrinsically stable enough to form from strands that carry no such preorganization, that is, from polyglycine. To offset the conformational entropy of a Gly-rich tract, we embedded Gly<sub>6</sub> within flanking triple-helical (Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>n</sub> clamps in Ac-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>6</sub>-Gly<sub>6</sub>-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>5</sub>-Pro-Hyp-NH<sub>2</sub> and compared it with an otherwise identical peptide in which Gly<sub>6</sub> was replaced by two [2-(2-aminoethoxy)ethoxy]acetic acid units, a flexible, length-matched spacer that lacks most of the regularly spaced backbone amides of Gly<sub>6</sub>. Circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the diagnostic positive band at 225 nm. The molar ellipticity of the spacer-containing control was 86% of that of the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, matching the 35/41 = 85% ratio of residues capable of triple-helix formation and consistent with the Gly<sub>6</sub> segment contributing to the triple-helical signal. Thermal denaturation yielded a T<sub>m</sub> of 46.8°C for the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, 6.3°C higher than that of the matched spacer control. This added stability indicates that the polyglycine tract is not merely accommodated within the helix but contributes stabilizing interstrand hydrogen bonds. Together, these data indicate that three polyglycine strands can form a collagen triple helix when flanked by triple-helical clamps. This result is consistent with the idea that the triple-helical architecture predates the recruitment of Pro and Hyp, informs the evolutionary origin of collagen, and offers a blunt-ended, symmetric scaffold for designing peptidic triple helices.

raw.abstractText:
While insulin activates the sympathetic nervous system in experimental settings, whether therapeutic insulin administration is associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance under free-living conditions remains unclear. This prospective observational study investigated the association between insulin dosing and cardiac autonomic balance in adults with type 1 diabetes managed exclusively with insulin therapy. Participants underwent continuous heart rate variability (HRV) and glucose monitoring over 4 consecutive days during routine daily activities. Cardiac sympathetic predominance was assessed using the low-frequency power to high-frequency power (LF/HF) ratio derived from HRV analysis, and associations were evaluated using generalized estimating equations. A higher last bolus insulin dose was associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the early sleep phase. A higher basal insulin dose was also associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the late sleep phase. These associations persisted after adjustment for mean glucose and mean absolute glucose change during the corresponding sleep phases. Under free-living conditions, higher insulin doses were associated with dose-dependent increases in cardiac sympathetic predominance, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing may be linked to cardiac autonomic regulation in individuals with type 1 diabetes, highlighting the importance of considering cardiac autonomic balance and potential cardiovascular risk when optimizing insulin therapy.

Article highlights

The relationship between therapeutic insulin administration and cardiac autonomic balance under free-living conditions remains unclear. We examined whether insulin dosing was associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance during daily life in adults with type 1 diabetes managed with insulin therapy. Higher last bolus and basal insulin doses were associated with increased cardiac sympathetic predominance during the early and late sleep phases, respectively, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing patterns may be linked to cardiac autonomic balance, with potential implications for optimizing insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Prolonged exposure to hepatotoxic antiretroviral therapy (ART) could lead to chronic liver injury, which might increase risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We used causal inference methods to evaluate if cumulative exposure to ART with known mechanisms of chronic liver injury is associated with HCC among people with HIV (PWH), by chronic liver disease (CLD) status.

Methods

We conducted a cohort study of antiretroviral-naive PWH with and without diagnosed CLD who initiated ART in the Veterans Affairs between 1999 and 2023. Exposure to ART with known mechanism of chronic liver injury (mitochondrial toxicity or accumulation of toxic intermediates) was determined monthly through prescription fills. Incident HCC was identified by Veterans Affairs National Cancer Registry and/or recorded diagnoses. Marginal structural models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of HCC associated with cumulative exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART compared with ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms, by CLD status.

Results

Among 11,854 PWH without CLD and 6771 PWH with CLD, we observed 112 and 378 HCC events, respectively. Among PWH without CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was associated with HCC when compared with ≥4 years of use of ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms (OR = 4.02 [95% CI: 1.00-16.24]). Among PWH with CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was not associated with HCC (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.68-2.72).

Conclusion

Four or more years of ART with a chronic liver injury mechanism was associated with HCC among PWH without CLD, but not those with CLD.

raw.abstractText: Melatonin (MEL) is an endogenous hormone that regulates circadian rhythm, immune function and oxidative stress responses. Norepinephrine (NE), an endogenous catecholamine, increases blood pressure through the sympathetic nervous system and is commonly administered intraoperatively or in the clinically ill patient for hemodynamic support. Although endogenous NE is known to stimulate MEL synthesis, the effects of exogenous intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentration, particularly under general anaesthesia (GA), remain poorly characterised. This study examined the influence of intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentrations in healthy volunteers, both awake and under general anaesthesia. A secondary analysis was conducted using data from a prospective, single-centre, cross-over study involving volunteers who received stepwise NE infusions while awake and under total intravenous general anaesthesia. Arterial blood samples were collected to determine plasma MEL and NE concentrations. Linear mixed-effects modelling was used to assess the relationship between NE and MEL concentrations. A total of 36 healthy volunteers were enroled, yielding 417 MEL-NE samples. Intravenous NE administration was significantly associated with higher plasma MEL concentration, corresponding to an estimated 26% increase in MEL per 1 standard-deviation increase in NE concentration (Estimate = 0.230, p < 0.001). MEL concentrations were approximately 43% higher in the awake phase compared to GA (Estimate = 0.356, p < 0.001). GA did not significantly modify the NE-MEL association (Estimate = -0.02877, p = 0.528). Substantial positive correlation was observed between baseline MEL concentrations and the magnitude of the response to NE administration (r = 0.74). In conclusion, intravenous NE increases plasma MEL concentrations in both awake and anaesthetised individuals. Substantial interindividual variation in MEL response suggests underlying physiological differences. Future studies should explore the long-term effects of NE administration on MEL concentrations. Objective

To compare serum total tau and α-synuclein among controls, drug-naïve children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and children with ADHD receiving methylphenidate.

Methods

Original ELISA spreadsheets provided 26 controls, 29 evaluable drug-naïve participants and 32 methylphenidate-treated participants. Boundary-coded results (> 500 pg/mL for tau; < 938 pg/mL for α-synuclein) were assigned the recorded boundary for rank-based analyses. Groups were compared using Kruskal-Wallis tests and Dunn-Bonferroni contrasts; within-group associations used Spearman correlations.

Results

α-Synuclein differed among groups (H = 49.859, p < 0.001, ε2 = 0.570), with all pairwise contrasts significant. Tau also differed (H = 10.492, p = 0.005, ε2 = 0.101); drug-naïve ADHD had lower tau than controls, whereas the treated group differed from neither comparator after correction. The α-synuclein-tau correlation remained significant after false-discovery-rate adjustment only in drug-naïve ADHD (ρ = 0.443, adjusted p = 0.048).

Conclusions

Serum α-synuclein and total tau showed distinct cross-sectional group patterns. These associations do not establish methylphenidate effects and require prospective confirmation.

raw.abstractText: TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK, the TAM receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), play roles in phagocytosis and negative regulation of immune responses, contributing to homeostasis in many adult tissues. Aberrant TAM signaling leads to diseases including autoimmune disorders, viral infection, inflammation, and cancer. Development of successful drugs targeting TAM receptors is hindered by incomplete knowledge of the receptor activation mechanism. Receptor dimerization is assumed to play a role, as seen for most RTKs. However, full biological responses require the TAM ligands to engage phosphatidylserine in an opposing cell or virus membrane, suggesting a more complex mechanism, possibly involving higher-order receptor oligomerization or clustering. Here, we present an X-ray crystal structure of the ectodomain of MERTK, which adopts a highly curved conformation with key interdomain boundaries stabilized by N-linked glycan moieties. We show that this MERTK extracellular region (ECR) forms a similar conformation in solution using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), which also suggests a flexible ECR. We compare these crystallographic and solution data for MERTK with SAXS and AlphaFold structural predictions for the other two TAM receptors. SAXS data confirm that each TAM ECR has a distinct curvature, with TYRO3 the most bent and AXL relatively straight. This leads us to speculate that these different ectodomain conformations guide receptor-specific functions. The MERTK X-ray crystal structure also suggests a head-to-tail intermolecular interaction between the Ig2 domain of one MERTK and the FNIIIb domain of a second that has intriguing parallels with interactions that have been proposed to regulate Eph receptor clustering.

raw.abstractText: Activity-guided separation of medicinal plants requires linking activity signals and chromatographic resolution in complex matrices. In this study, based on a previously established HPLC-DPPH platform, medium-pressure prefractionation and preparative chromatographic purification were applied for the targeted isolation of free radical scavengers from Saxifraga tangutica (S. tangutica). raw.abstractText: Ripened washed-rind and long-ripened cheeses owe their prized sulfurous, savory character to intensive proteolysis and amino-acid catabolism; the same activity, when poorly controlled, also generates sensory off-flavors and toxic biogenic amines (BAs). Histamine and tyramine reach up to approximately 2000-2500 and 1000-2000 mg/kg in extreme samples, although most cheeses contain far less, so that a 30-g portion of a high-histamine cheese can exceed the 50-mg per-meal intake regarded as without adverse effect in healthy adults. Flavor formation and chemical safety have traditionally been studied apart. This critical review reframes them as two outcomes of one metabolism: Proteolysis liberates a shared free amino-acid pool from which volatile sulfur compounds (VSCs) and BAs arise. Because the principal VSCs derive from methionine whereas the major BAs derive from histidine, tyrosine, ornithine, arginine, and lysine, we treat the branches not as direct competitors for one substrate but as metabolically coupled fates linked by shared proteolytic supply, overlapping physicochemical controls and microbial cross-feeding. Integrating evidence across cheese families, we reclassify the ripening microbiota into condition-dependent functional guilds, formalize metabolic bivalence (organisms that both generate flavor and degrade amines), and define a sensory inflection point separating the windowed VSC dose-response from the monotonic BA hazard. We critically appraise multi-omics, volatilomics, biosensors, machine learning, and digital twins, and outline a precision-fermentation roadmap. Current, largely in vitro, and single-variety evidence is consistent with, but does not establish, controllable decoupling, which we frame as a testable hypothesis that recasts cheese quality as a controllable metabolic-allocation problem.

raw.abstractText: Drug-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remains a major challenge in drug development and clinical practice, often resulting in treatment interruption, drug attrition, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. DIC has been associated with a wide range of therapeutic agents, including anthracyclines, HER2-targeted therapies, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and other cardiotoxic drugs. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have attracted increasing attention as stable and versatile regulatory RNAs involved in cardiovascular injury. This review summarizes the biogenesis and functional mechanisms of circRNAs, their pathological roles in DIC, biomarker potential, therapeutic implications, and translational challenges. CircRNAs regulate gene expression through diverse mechanisms, including miRNA sequestration, interactions with RNA-binding proteins, transcriptional regulation, modulation of alternative splicing, and, in some cases, peptide translation. These regulatory functions have been implicated in apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, pyroptosis, and cardiac remodeling during DIC. Emerging evidence suggests that circRNAs may serve as candidate molecular markers and potential therapeutic targets for DIC. However, the current evidence is derived predominantly from cellular and animal models, with doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity accounting for a substantial proportion of available studies. Clinical validation, particularly in well-characterized patient cohorts and across different drug classes, remains limited. Overall, further efforts are needed to establish standardized circRNA detection and quantification methods, validate their functional roles, conduct prospective clinical studies, and determine their incremental value in combination with established cardiac biomarkers before circRNA-based approaches can be translated into clinical management of DIC.

raw.abstractText: Vitamin D is a nutrient and prohormone obtained from diet and supplements and synthesized in the skin. It is essential for calcium and phosphate homeostasis and skeletal health and influences multiple extra-skeletal processes, yet deficiency remains common worldwide. This narrative review summarizes vitamin D sources, physiology, metabolism, pharmacokinetics, clinical relevance and safety and outlines the distinct pharmacokinetic profiles and clinical roles of vitamin D, calcidiol and calcitriol and its analogues. Evidence consistently supports vitamin D, combined with calcium, for preventing and treating deficiency-related skeletal disorders in high-risk populations, and in specific conditions such as malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism and frailty. In vitamin D-replete populations, large trials show limited extra-skeletal benefits, apart from modest effects on cancer mortality and progression from prediabetes to Type 2 diabetes. Untargeted screening is not recommended. Future research should prioritize targeted supplementation, standardized assays and identification of populations most likely to benefit from supplementation.

raw.title: Semaglutide Increases Striatal Leptin Sensitivity, Impacting Dopaminergic Response to Cocaine
raw.authorString: Muldowney JJ, Umlauf MC, Bocarsly ME.
raw.abstractText: There is accumulating evidence that the GLP-1 analog, semaglutide, might effectively curb intake of cocaine via brain dopaminergic functioning, despite limited brain penetrance. However, there is currently no established mechanism elucidating how chronic semaglutide treatment regulates the dopaminergic response to cocaine. Cocaine is a highly addictive substance that produces rewarding effects primarily through antagonism of the dopamine transporter (DAT). Therapeutics for cocaine use disorder (CUD) have long targeted DAT in the hope of reducing cocaine intake. Metabolic hormones such as leptin and insulin have been shown to influence DAT, and for that reason have been explored for the regulation of cocaine reward and behavior. Interestingly, while semaglutide does not penetrate the brain, it does peripherally modulate metabolic hormones that enter the brain. Through fast-scan cyclic voltammetry and behavioral experimentation, we examined the effects of chronic semaglutide treatment on dopamine signaling, cocaine-induced dopamine release, and locomotor sensitivity. We determined that chronic semaglutide inhibits dopaminergic reward induced by cocaine. Surprisingly, semaglutides effects on cocaine reward were blunted in mice fasted overnight, suggesting a mechanistic dependence on metabolic hormones. Semaglutide administration generated significant reductions in fasting blood leptin, as well as enhanced striatal leptin sensitivity compared to vehicle controls. Preceding cocaine exposure, application of leptin to fasted mice restored semaglutides regulation of cocaine. Our results exhibit a potential mechanism for semaglutide-induced cocaine reward inhibition, emphasizing the potential of central leptin signaling as a therapeutic target for CUD.

raw.title: Lipid-Based Nanocarriers for Oral Nutraceutical Delivery: Absorption Mechanisms, Manufacturing Routes and a Critical Appraisal of the Human Pharmacokinetic Evidence
raw.authorString: Ng KP.
raw.abstractText: Many widely used nutraceuticals, including curcuminoids, polyphenols, carotenoids, coenzyme Q10 and labile vitamins, reach the systemic circulation poorly after oral intake because of low solubility, gastrointestinal degradation, efflux and presystemic conjugation. Lipid-based nanocarriers have become the leading commercial solution. This narrative review examines liposomes, niosomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, nanoemulsions, micelles and self-emulsifying systems for nutraceutical delivery. It explains the three mechanisms by which lipid excipients raise absorption (mixed-micelle solubilisation, lymphatic transport and modulation of enterocyte handling), compares carrier classes on composition, stability and manufacturability, and examines the conversion of liquid dispersions into stable powders, using spray-dried liposomal vitamin C as a worked example. Human pharmacokinetic studies are tabulated and critically appraised. Reported gains range from about 1.3-fold to more than 180-fold, but this spread reflects study design as much as technology: measurement of total rather than unconjugated analyte, unequal comparator doses, small industry-funded cohorts and few head-to-head comparisons. In the most rigorous equal-dose comparison of eight curcumin formulations, only micellar and cyclodextrin products outperformed native curcumin. The review proposes critical quality attributes for lipid-based ingredients and a minimum reporting standard for future bioavailability trials.

raw.authorString: Ridoy M.
raw.abstractText: Problematic social media use has emerged as a significant global public health concern, particularly among university students. This systematic review synthesizes contemporary evidence across diverse geographical contexts to evaluate the relationship between social media addiction and objective sleep quality parameters. Following strict inclusion criteria, ten high-quality empirical studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses published between 2023 and 2026—representing populations in Bangladesh, China, India, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom, Nigeria, and Brazil—were synthesized. The collective findings across a cumulative sample size of over 40,000 participants demonstrate a robust, negative correlation between excessive digital exposure and sleep duration. Late-night screen time, driven by Fear of Missing Out (FoMo) and digital fatigue, severely alters circadian rhythms and suppresses melatonin secretion, leading to fragmented sleep, daytime sleepiness, and heightened depressive symptoms. While protective behavioral strategies like physical exercise offer a viable mitigation buffer, their efficacy is heavily undermined by extreme digital dependencies. In conclusion, unregulated social media consumption poses an escalating threat to student well-being. Immediate multi-sectoral interventions, digital literacy programs, and campus-based health policies are required to safeguard the physical and psychological health of the higher education workforce.

raw.authorString: Avula B, Katragunta K, Tatapudi KK, Bae J, Chittiboyina AG, Khan IA.
raw.abstractText:
Background:

High-concentration 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products have been described by the US Food and Drug Administration as an emerging public health concern, and in August 2026 the Drug Enforcement Administration temporarily placed mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MP), MGM-15 (dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine), and MGM-16 in schedule I. Since July, Utah and Tennessee officials have reported overdoses, deaths, and laboratory findings involving tablets labeled as cat's claw (Uncaria tomentosa), an herbal supplement without known opioid activity. Chemical data on such products are scarce, and consumers cannot tell from the label which opioid-active compounds they contain.

Methods:

In a cross-sectional analysis, we purchased 46 chewable or unit-dose products labeled as containing cat's claw from online retailers and 3 gas stations in Mississippi during September 2026. The products represented 17 brands. Methanol extracts were analyzed by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography with photodiode array detection and compared with a methanol extract of botanically verified U tomentosa bark. Liquid chromatography quadrupole time of flight mass spectrometry identified additional compounds, and compounds were quantified against authentic reference standards. Proportions are reported with exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% CIs.

Results:

None of the 46 products declared kratom alkaloids or their derivatives, yet all contained at least one component. Mitragynine was quantified in 41 products (89%; 95% CI, 76% to 96%), 7-OH in 35 (76%; 95% CI, 61% to 87%), MGM-15 in 24 (52%; 95% CI, 37% to 67%), and MP in 22 (48%; 95% CI, 33% to 63%). A total of 39 products (85%; 95% CI, 71% to 94%) contained MP or MGM-15, which are temporarily controlled in schedule I. Tianeptine, an antidepressant not approved in the US, was present in five products (11%; 95% CI, 4% to 24%) at 27.9 to 40.2 mg per unit. The 7-OH content ranged from 0.01 to 95.4 mg per unit. Eight products carrying claims such as "NO KRATOM and No 7-OH" or "NO 7-OH" contained mitragynine, 7-OH, and 3-dehydromitragynine.

Conclusions:

Labels gave consumers no reliable guide to exposure. Clinicians evaluating unexplained opioid toxicity after use of a cat's claw product should consider kratom-derived opioids and tianeptine. Regulators may need product testing and label enforcement in addition to scheduling of individual compounds.

raw.abstractText: The leaves of Psidium guajava L. (guava) are an underutilized resource containing diverse bioactive metabolites. The present study evaluated the inhibitory potential of P. guajava leaf fractions against two SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets: the Spike RBD–ACE2 interaction of the Wuhan and Omicron BA.1 variants, and 3CLpro enzymatic activity. A methanolic extract was fractionated by vacuum liquid chromatography, and fraction F14 was then separated into subfractions F14A–F14D through the use of Sephadex LH-20. F14 and its subfractions inhibited the Spike RBD–ACE2 interaction of the Wuhan variant, whereas against Omicron BA.1, all fractions showed IC₅₀ values <1.25 mg mL−1. F14, F14C, and F14D also inhibited 3CLpro, with IC₅₀ values <1.25 mg mL−1. F14D demonstrated the most consistent inhibitory profile across all the three targets and was selected for further characterization by LC–HRMS. The three major constituents were tentatively assigned as a myricetin hexoside, a quercetin hexoside, and a quercetin pentoside. Overall, the results of this study suggest that F14D contains bioactive constituents with potential inhibitory activity against SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets, although further studies are required to determine their antiviral activity.

raw.authorString: Xie Y, Pi Z.
raw.abstractText: Objective Preeclampsia continues to be a primary cause of health complications and death for expectant mothers and their unborn children. Early identification of pregnant women at risk, followed by timely preventive interventions, carries clear clinical value. We examined whether the serum uric acid to creatinine ratio (UA/Cr) measured at admission is associated with preeclampsia and whether it adds discriminative value when used in machine learning (ML) models. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using the MIMIC-IV database, identifying 4,756 pregnant women with gestational age ≥ 20 weeks; 4,247 were excluded for missing data, leaving 509 for analysis (78 preeclampsia cases, 431 controls). Preeclampsia was identified by ICD-9/10 codes. UA/Cr (uric acid mg/dL ÷ creatinine mg/dL, first admission-day value) entered logistic regression as both a continuous variable and a quartile variable (Q1 as reference), with two adjustment sets: Model 1 adjusted for age, and Model 2 for age, language, and red blood cell count. Restricted cubic splines characterized nonlinearity, and subgroup analyses tested robustness. Six machine learning algorithms—random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, AdaBoost, and TabPFN—were trained on the training set (n = 355) and validated on the validation set (n = 154). Features were selected by univariate screening, variance inflation factor (VIF) diagnostics, and LASSO.Univariate analysis for screening, VIF diagnostics, and LASSO were utilized to choose features. Result UA/Cr rose with preeclampsia risk and the dose–response curve was approximately linear (nonlinearity P = 0.911): each 1-unit increment was associated with an OR of 1.184 (95% CI 1.061–1.320, P = 0.002). The highest quartile carried an OR of 2.758 versus the lowest quartile (95% CI 1.318–6.128, P = 0.009; trend P = 0.020). AUCs in the validation set ranged from 0.655 to 0.761 (LightGBM the highest), with UA/Cr ranking second in feature importance. The four top-performing models did not differ significantly from one another. Conclusion In this MIMIC-IV cohort of hospitalized pregnant women, a higher admission UA/Cr was associated with preeclampsia, and an ML model built from routine admission data achieved moderate concurrent discrimination. Because of the cross-sectional design, the analysis does not support prospective prediction. Prospective and external validation, alongside head-to-head comparison with absolute uric acid, is required before any clinical use in risk stratification.

Background

Clinic workflow efficiency influences patient and employee satisfaction, impacting effective delivery of care. Utilizing lean methodology, we aim to increase the percentage of patients seen within 15 minutes of scheduled appointment to 75% and reduce nonvalue-added time (NVT) per visit by half within 6 months.

Methods

Frontline stakeholders observed workflow inefficiencies in an outpatient general surgery clinic, leading to long wait times and generalized dissatisfaction. From August to September 2023, patient and staff flow was captured and appointment component time intervals observed. Only 35.8% of patients were seen within 15 minutes of appointment, with median appointment-to-seen time (AST) 19.00 minutes and NVT 74%. Interventions were implemented through progressive plan-do-study-act (PDSA) cycles, including changes to workflow, rooming, and scheduling template. Appointment time interval data were collected and analyzed using run charts.

Results

PDSA 1 yielded median AST of 15.68 minutes, with 51.7% of patients seen within 15 minutes of appointment. PDSA 2 resulted in a median AST of 8.00 minutes, with 66.4% of patients seen within 15 minutes of appointment and reduced median NVT from 74% to 55.9%. Late in PDSA 2 in December, when the clinic was short-staffed, both median AST and NVT increased. PDSA 3 resulted in reduced median AST of 5.00 minutes, with 82.9% of patients seen within 15 minutes of appointment and reduced median NVT to 51.5%, with improved performance stability particularly with respect to AST.

Conclusions

Utilization of lean methodology with multiple targeted workflow and scheduling interventions resulted in improved efficiency in an outpatient general surgery clinic.

papers.title: Contrasting potassium responses of growth, magnesium status and steviol glycoside traits in Stevia rebaudiana

raw.title: Contrasting potassium responses of growth, magnesium status and steviol glycoside traits in Stevia rebaudiana
raw.authorString: Chen H, Liu J, Ye S, Shen J, Jiang C.
raw.abstractText: Background: Potassium (K) is essential for stevia production, but increasing K beyond sufficiency may not simultaneously improve root growth, harvestable biomass, magnesium (Mg) nutrition, and steviol glycoside production. This study examined whether these traits share a common response across a broad K gradient in Stevia rebaudiana . Results: Plants of ‘Tiannong 5’ were grown at five nutrient-solution K concentrations of 1, 4, 8, 16, and 24 mmol L -1 . Root architecture, biomass, leaf and root K–Mg status, and 13 steviol glycosides were quantified, and treatment comparisons were integrated with restricted dose–response models and bootstrap-derived response ranges. Intermediate K supported root expansion and whole-plant biomass. Root length and whole-plant dry weight had model-estimated peaks at 4.69 and 5.38 mmol L -1 K, with 90% high-response ranges of 2.88–7.65 and 3.17–9.16 mmol L -1 , respectively. Leaf dry weight differed among treatments but showed no supported continuous optimum. Leaf Mg concentration declined from 1.769 to 0.896 mg g -1 as K increased, accompanied by lower leaf Mg content and a higher leaf K/Mg molar ratio. Neither total steviol glycoside concentration nor content per plant showed a supported K breakpoint. Their observed means at K24 were 9.05% and 20.54% lower than those at K16, respectively. In contrast, the rebaudioside A/stevioside ratio increased with K supply, indicating divergent responses of glycoside composition and total productivity. The candidate K16–K24 interval corresponded to fitted leaf Mg concentrations of approximately 0.9–1.1 mg g -1 , but this treatment-level association does not represent a diagnostic Mg threshold. Conclusions: Root expansion, biomass accumulation, Mg status, glycoside productivity, and glycoside composition showed distinct K-response patterns. Once K supply exceeded the intermediate range supporting root and whole-plant growth, further K provided diminishing production returns, intensified leaf K–Mg imbalance, and failed to sustain total steviol glycoside productivity. These findings provide a rationale for independently testing coordinated K–Mg nutrition as a strategy to sustain stevia leaf and glycoside production.

raw.title: Insights into the Structural, Electrical, Optical, and Dielectric Characteristics of Magnesium-Decorated Lanthanum Ferrite (La<sub>0.75</sub>Mg<sub>0.25</sub>FeO<sub>3</sub>) by the Sol-Gel Method
raw.authorString: Tahir S, Ijaz E.
raw.abstractText: Ferrites are ceramic products made mostly of iron oxide mixed with other metal oxides, like cobalt, nickel, zinc, or manganese. They are frequently employed as a fundamental substance in the electrical and electronics sectors because of their variable magnetic features, relatively low eddy-current distortion at elevated frequencies, and excellent electrical resistance. Lanthanum ferrite (LaFeO3) has unique electrical, optical, and dielectric characteristics, along with high chemical stability, making it a viable perovskite-type material. Magnesium replacement can affect the crystalline structure, defect chemistry, and charge transfer pathways in order to vary its functionality. Mg replacement affects the structural, dielectric, electrical, and optical properties of La2-xMgxFeO3 metallic materials, as previous studies have shown. The goal of the present research is to use the sol-gel technique to manufacture La0.75Mg0.25FeO3 and examine its structural, electrical, optical, and dielectric properties for prospective applications in sensors, photocatalysis, electronic equipment, telecommunications, and shielding purposes. In order to comprehend the impact of the magnesium substitution process on the material's (La0.75Mg0.25FeO3) structural characteristics and analyze its capability for anticipated purposes. The research intends to analyze crystalline phase development, crystallite dimensions, morphological characteristics, a standard optical spectrum width, electrical conductivity, and temperature-varying dielectric activity. The sol-gel method was used to create a set of magnesium-doped lanthanum ferrites La0.75Mg0.25FeO3, which were then sintered at different temperatures that is 100°C, 300°C, 600°C, and 900 °C. In this study, XRD analysis confirmed the orthorhombic phase of La0.75Mg0.25FeO3. The most noticeable peak (110) exhibits switching, and the average crystallite (D) size falls between 7.2 and 8.5 nm. With rising annealing temperatures, the X-ray density (ρx) progressively dropped from 7.27 to 6.88 g/cm2, whereas the dislocation density (δ) steadily increased from 4.2 to 5.2×1015 lines/m2 as the temperature rose. The large surface area (7.5 to 13.6 m2/g) suggests the use of supercapacitors and other energy storage devices. As annealing temperature rises, a decreasing pattern in the direct band gap (4.09 to 3.87 eV) and indirect transition (3.33 to 3.13 eV) has been noted. The low value of the refractive index (0.1 to 0.3) means these nano-materials can be utilized in making cladding of fiber optics and in solar cells to make an anti-reflection coating layer. SEM results showed the non-homogeneous morphology.

papers.title: A brain signature of vaping cue-elicited craving

raw.title: A brain signature of vaping cue-elicited craving
raw.authorString: Zhao S, Yu H, Koban L, Wang Y, Peng Q, Ye T, Amlung M, MacKillop J, Sweet L, Liu J.
raw.abstractText: E-cigarette use among young adults has grown rapidly, raising concerns about nicotine dependence and motivating a better understanding of the neurobiology of vaping. We used a cue-induced craving fMRI paradigm to develop and evaluate a brain signature of vaping cue-elicited craving, and to compare it with smoking- and food-craving signatures developed using the same analytic pipeline. Using LASSO-PCR with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, we identified a distributed pattern of brain activity that reliably predicted normative vaping craving from an independent sample (hereafter, normative craving). The vaping-craving signature was also substantially distinct from smoking- and food-craving signatures, both spatially and functionally, and showed specificity relative to previously established craving signatures. Moreover, greater signature expression was associated with greater e-cigarette dependence severity and showed a positive, though modest, prospective association with daily puff counts over four weeks, demonstrating the signature's behavioral and clinical relevance. Together, these findings establish a cross-validated brain signature of vaping cue-elicited craving, demonstrate its differentiation from other craving-related neural patterns, and link its expression to e-cigarette dependence and real-world use. More broadly, they support the potential of this framework for developing reproducible neural markers of craving.

raw.title: Resveratrol Modulates Inflammatory Gene Expression in LPS Stimulated HMC3 Microglia
raw.authorString: Kooshali AE, Kazemi M, Arabi Z, Abolmashadi F, Yazdi FHH, Rafinezhad N, Nazemi K, Nemati M, Mirzaei B, Turk Z, Norouzi F, Mahmoudian SA, Rouzbahani KA.
raw.abstractText: Background Activated by LPS, the signaling pathway of TLR4 is triggered in microglial cells, leading to a dramatic increase in the production of inflammatory mediators (IL1B, TNF, CXCL10, and CCL2). Although resveratrol (RSV) has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory effects, its concentration- and time-dependent effects on multiple inflammatory transcripts in human HMC3 microglial cells remain incompletely characterized. Objective This study aimed to characterize the dose- and time-dependent effects of resveratrol on IL1B, TNF, CXCL10, and CCL2 expression in LPS-stimulated HMC3 human microglial cells. Methods We treated HMC3 cells with LPS (100 ng/mL) and then challenged them with RSV. Dose–response experiments employed 5, 10, and 20 µM RSV for 24 h. We performed time-course analysis using 10 µM RSV at 6, 12, and 24 h. We quantified mRNA levels by SYBR Green qRT-PCR using the 2⁻ΔΔCt method, with GAPDH as a reference gene. Statistical comparisons were conducted by one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s post hoc test (p < 0.05). Results RSV caused a concentration- and time-dependent inhibition of LPS-induced inflammatory gene expression. The highest inhibition was obtained at 10 µM RSV after 24 hours, with IL1B and TNF being inhibited to 50–60% (p < 0.01) and CXCL10 and CCL2 to 65–75% (p < 0.05) of LPS-induced levels. An additional increase to 20 µM RSV did not increase inhibition, indicating a plateau effect. The time-course experiment demonstrated a gradual inhibition of transcription, with maximal effects at 24 hours. Conclusion Resveratrol reduced LPS-induced expression of IL1B, TNF, CXCL10, and CCL2 in HMC3 human microglial cells, with the greatest transcriptional effects observed at 10 µM after 24 hours. These findings support a concentration- and time-associated anti-inflammatory effect of resveratrol at the transcriptional level. However, because we did not directly assess signaling pathways, protein expression, or cell viability, further studies are needed to establish the underlying mechanisms and determine the relationship between transcriptional suppression and cellular function.

raw.title: Ascorbate is a physiological tumor suppressor metabolite in leukemia
raw.authorString: Wijshake T, Rose J, Jun JH, Kwarteng EO, Yang X, Zielke J, Mahesula S, Li L, Chung SS, Comazzetto S, Morrison SJ, Chen W, Agathocleous M.
raw.abstractText: Accumulation of oncometabolites promotes tumorigenesis, but it is not known if there are naturally occurring tumor suppressor metabolites whose deficiency within cancer-initiating cells causes cancer. Many leukemia patients are ascorbate deficient. Here we show that hematopoietic-specific ascorbate depletion in mice is sufficient to cause or promote leukemogenesis. Hematopoietic-specific ascorbate depletion promoted leukemogenesis by acting within leukemia initiating cells. Ascorbate depletion in myeloid leukemia expanded plasmacytoid dendritic cells, an effect mediated by the ascorbate molecular targets TET2 and TET3. Leukemia cells accumulated ascorbate as part of a tumor suppressor response to neoplastic proliferation that limited progression but depleted circulating ascorbate. Ascorbate restoration in mice with established leukemias extended survival. Hematopoietic-specific ascorbate depletion caused leukemia in collaboration with TET2 loss and was sufficient to cause leukemia with high penetrance even in the absence of other engineered mutations. These results identify ascorbate as a physiological tumor suppressor metabolite in blood cancers.

raw.abstractText:
Purpose

Liver fibrosis induced by cholestasis involves oxidative stress and activation of hepatic stellate cells. Astaxanthin (ASX), a potent antioxidant, may modulate this pathological process. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of ASX on cholestasis-induced fibrosis in a bile duct ligation (BDL) rat model.

Methods

Male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to three groups: sham-operated, BDL with no treatment (NT), and BDL treated with ASX (100 mg/kg/day orally for 20 days). On day 21 post-surgery, liver and serum samples were collected. Biochemical assays, histological staining, immunohistochemistry, and quantitative PCR were performed to assess liver function, fibrosis, inflammation, and expression of aquaporins (AQP) and multidrug resistance-associated protein (MRP) transporters.

Results

The ASX group showed significantly improved body weight gain and serum albumin compared to the NT group. While liver enzymes and bilirubin remained elevated, AQP8 expression was partially restored, and MRP3 was further upregulated by ASX. Although the degree of NF-κB staining grade and histological fibrosis grade in NT group was significantly higher than those in sham group, no significant differences were observed between sham group and ASX group.

Conclusion

The postoperative administration of ASX induced beneficial effects, resulting in the reduction of hepatic fibrosis via mechanisms involving the inhibition of NF-κB expression and improvement of AQP8 expression and enhancement of compensatory MRP3 activity.

raw.authorString: Porter A, Abdul Azim A, Lwande JS, Vause CV, Kittle Jr JK, Peskin S, Shotorbani KR.
raw.abstractText: Isolate-based antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) is highly reproducible across workflows, laboratories, and institutions. While the basis of the test is remarkably consistent, multiple constraints may obscure clinically relevant diversity and resistant subpopulations. Exponentially increasing rates of antimicrobial resistance have created a desire for faster AST methods to decrease empiric antimicrobial treatment in the hope of reducing both treatment failure and further development of resistance. This review evaluates the limitations of conventional isolate-based AST including colony selection bias, population diversity loss, and heteroresistance and assesses several new rapid phenotypic AST methods through the lens of those limitations and biases.

To better assess the variability of solar energy at the Earth's surface, an emerging metric for predicting the clear sky index (\( K_{t}^{\ast } \)) and its increments (\( ∆K_{t}^{\ast } \)) is used. It concludes that there is a mass reduction of increments, mainly those > 0, which are corrected for stabilization of PV production, even on intermediate days with emerging characteristics of clear and cloudy skies. With the rectification of fluctuations to reduce attenuation, it proves viable for modeling rectified output power in k-central units, maximizing their lifetime.

raw.abstractText:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of levetiracetam versus valproate in children with new-onset or previously treated but inadequately controlled epilepsy.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library from inception to April 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing levetiracetam versus valproate in children (aged 0-18 years) with new-onset or previously treated but inadequately controlled epilepsy. Outcomes included seizure freedom, exploratory analyses of survival time without seizure and time to first seizure recurrence, change in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, and adverse events.

Results

Eight RCTs involving 1,000 participants were included. Seizure freedom did not differ significantly between treatments (5 studies, 655 participants; RR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.83-1.09; P = 0.45; I² = 59.5%; low-certainty evidence). Exploratory time-related outcomes favored valproate but were limited by low-certainty evidence and inadequate handling of censoring. Levetiracetam was associated with lower AST levels, although this did not establish superior hepatic safety, and with fewer overall adverse events and less weight gain.

Conclusions

No significant difference in seizure freedom was detected between levetiracetam and valproate, although the low-certainty finding was sensitive to one trial. Time-related outcomes favored valproate but were exploratory and limited by inadequate handling of censoring. Levetiracetam was associated with fewer overall adverse events and less weight gain, while behavioral and hepatic safety remained uncertain. Treatment should be individualized based on patient and medication-related factors.

raw.title: Variation in psychiatric diagnoses and use of psychotropic medication among children, adolescents, and young adults in Denmark
raw.authorString: Sonne H, Kildegaard H, Bech M, Wesselhoeft R, Hansen ASK, Ording AG, Pottegaard A.
raw.abstractText:
Background:

Psychiatric diagnoses and psychotropic medication use among children, adolescents, and young adults have increased in high-income countries, with concerns about geographic variation. We described national trends and geographic variation in Denmark from 2010 to 2025 and developed an interactive online tool to explore these patterns. Methods We conducted a nationwide, descriptive, repeated cross-sectional register-based study of all Danish residents aged 0-24 years in 2010-2025 (n=2,930,744), using the Danish National Patient Registry and the Danish National Prescription Registry. We estimated annual incidence, prevalence, and, for selected diagnoses, lifetime prevalence, by age and sex, and age- and sex-standardised rates across regions, health councils, and municipalities. We assessed geographic variation using deviations from national means, coefficients of variation, Gini coefficients, and funnel plots. Findings Psychiatric diagnoses and psychotropic medication use increased from 2010 to 2025. The annual prevalence of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) increased from 0.41 to 2.3 per 100 individuals, autism spectrum disorders from 0.20 to 1.2, and melatonin use from 0.14 to 3.0. ADHD and autism spectrum disorders were more prevalent among boys and anxiety disorders among girls. Sertraline use was also more prevalent among girls. Geographic variation was observed across diagnoses and psychotropic medications at regional, health council, and municipal levels. For example, lifetime prevalence of autism ranged from 1.3 to 5.9 per 100 across municipalities, and in 2025 regional coefficients of variation ranged from 0.11 (sertraline) to 0.41 (atomoxetine). Results can be explored in the interactive online tool (https://bupstat.sdu.dk/?lang=en). Interpretation Psychiatric diagnoses and psychotropic medication use increased among Danish children, adolescents, and young adults, with marked geographic variation. Descriptive data cannot establish the causes of this variation, but the findings identify areas for further review and support continued monitoring. raw.abstractText: A comprehensive understanding of chemical changes in blood and bloodstains exposed to ex vivo environments remain limited. In this study, we evaluated the analytical validity window of metabolite analysis in ex vivo bloodstains by tracking chemical changes over 12 months. Bloodstains from a discovery set of 14 participants were analyzed at monthly intervals from Month 0 to Month 12 using LC-MS/MS nontargeted analysis. A total of 2,210 molecular features (MFs) were filtered, of which 270 MFs persisted continuously throughout the 12-month period. Principal component analysis, hierarchical clustering, and correlation analysis showed that the most pronounced changes to MF-levels occurred within the first two months, with the majority of baseline-derived MFs disappearing between Month 0 and Month 2. Five identified metabolites (choline, 5'-AMP, pyroglutamic acid, aspartic acid, and ornithine) were then quantified by targeted analysis in an independent validation set of 40 participants, with concentrations expressed as median [IQR]. Choline increased significantly from Month 0 and remained elevated throughout the 12 months, supporting its potential utility as a candidate long-term marker for distinguishing fresh blood from aged bloodstains. 5'-AMP changed significantly only within the first four months; the remaining three metabolites showed only minor fluctuations with no significant pairwise differences. These findings indicate that MF-level changes primarily reflect loss of baseline-derived MFs and were most pronounced within the initial two months. Individual targeted metabolites follow distinct trajectories and more gradual, irregular changes continue thereafter. This study provides foundational insights for the application of metabolomics to forensic bloodstain analysis.

raw.title: Redox–Immune Crosstalk After Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage: Neutrophil–Macrophage Dynamics, Antioxidant Strategies, and Muscle Regeneration
raw.authorString: Mănescu DC, Vărzaru CG, Tudor V, Mujea AM.
raw.abstractText: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) initiates a coordinated response in which redox signaling and innate immunity jointly shape tissue clearance, inflammatory resolution, and muscle regeneration. Oxidants generated by contracting myofibres, vascular and stromal cells, and recruited leukocytes can amplify membrane and molecular injury when insufficiently controlled, but they also regulate immune-cell recruitment, phagocytosis, efferocytosis, satellite-cell activity, and adaptive remodeling. This critical review integrates evidence on the temporal and spatial crosstalk among reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, neutrophils, monocytes/macrophages, endogenous antioxidant systems, and the regenerative niche after EIMD. Human studies document post-exercise changes in circulating leukocytes and intramuscular immune markers, yet direct cell-specific measurements of redox activity and regeneration remain scarce; most causal mechanisms derive from animal and cellular experiments. The review proposes a time-resolved redox–immune relay encompassing damage sensing, neutrophil-dominant amplification and clearance, monocyte/macrophage reprogramming, inflammatory resolution, and tissue remodeling. Macrophage behavior is treated as a dynamic multidimensional continuum rather than a binary M1/M2 sequence. Seven falsifiable propositions operationalize the framework. They predict that antioxidant effects depend on dose, timing, chemical target, tissue compartment, baseline redox status, and injury severity, and that improvements in soreness, creatine kinase, cytokines, or bulk oxidative markers are insufficient to establish enhanced regeneration. Available evidence does not support indiscriminate suppression of post-exercise oxidation. Instead, interventions should be evaluated by their capacity to constrain pathological oxidation while preserving redox-dependent immune and regenerative signaling.

Rationale & objective

Spot urine protein-to-creatinine (UPCR) and albumin-to-creatinine (UACR) ratios are common surrogates for 24-hour excretion, but their validity during acute kidney injury (AKI) is uncertain because kidney function is not at steady state. This study assessed the validity of these spot ratios during active AKI compared to after its resolution.

Study design

A prospective paired cohort study.

Setting & participants

One hundred hospitalized adult patients with AKI at a single center in Thailand.

Exposure

Active phase of AKI was the period between diagnosis and resolution, which was defined as the return of serum creatinine to baseline or a value ≥50% below the peak value, sustained for ≥48 hours.

Outcomes

The agreement and reliability between protein-to-creatine and albumin-to-creatinine ratios in spot urine samples versus in 24-hour urine collections.

Analytical approach

Agreement was evaluated using Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman analysis to quantify systematic bias and random error. Limits of Agreement (LoA) were defined as the range within which 95% of the differences between the two measurement methods were expected to fall.

Results

Spot ratios differed from 24-hour collections during AKI (CCC: UACR 0.81; UPCR 0.68) and became more reliable after recovery, (CCC: UACR 0.89; UPCR 0.83) (p=0.001). Limits of agreement were wide during AKI (UACR 0.22 to 8.37; UPCR 0.31 to 7.99) and narrowed significantly upon resolution (UACR 0.40 to 5.48; UPCR 0.47 to 4.91). Spot ratios systematically overestimated the 24-hour collections by 36% to 56% both during and after resolution of AKI. The unreliability of the spot urine values was most pronounced in patients with preserved baseline kidney function, severe AKI, and hemodynamic etiologies.

Limitations

Defining resolution via serum creatinine may not reflect complete resolution of AKI. The exclusively hospitalized cohort may limit generalizability to milder AKI occurring in the outpatient setting.

Conclusions

Spot urine ratios exhibit significant imprecision during active AKI compared to following its resolution. Clinicians should exercise caution when using these data to establish baseline proteinuria or monitor treatment response during AKI.

raw.abstractText:
Objective:

Amphetamine (AMP) and its derivates are commonly prescribed for the management of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This study aimed to 1) quantify AMP's transfer into human milk in lactating women receiving therapeutic doses and 2) contextualize infant exposure.

Methods:

Milk samples and dyad health histories of thirteen lactating women treated with varying doses of either mixed AMP, dextroamphetamine, or lisdexamfetamine were released for this study from the InfantRisk Human Milk Biorepository. Milk drug concentrations were quantified by validated liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and used to calculate standard relative infant dose (RIDmat) and RID standardized to the defined daily dose (RIDDDD) of 15 mg AMP base.

Results:

Average milk concentrations (Cavg) of AMP base ranged from 23.3 to 297.0 ng/mL and increased linearly (R^2 = 0.92) with maternal daily dose. The RIDmat ranged 3.6-10.8% and RIDDDD ranged 1.4-21.8%. The fitted regression line crossed the 10% RIDDDD threshold at 1.17x DDD, with the upper 95% prediction limit crossing at 0.84x DDD. No adverse event reported by the mother-infant dyads were attributed to AMP exposure, notably including absence of reduced milk supply.

Conclusions:

The levels of AMP observed in human milk followed a dose predictable manner. The average patient was predicted to remain below the 10% RID DDD safety threshold at total daily doses at or below approximately 28 mg of mixed AMP salts or 59 mg of lisdexamfetamine. Ninety-five percent of patients were predicted to remain below the threshold at or below approximately 20 mg and 40 mg, respectively.

Background

Tic disorders frequently co-occur with neurodevelopmental conditions, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, the impact of ASD on tic phenomenology, severity, and treatment patterns remains incompletely understood.

Objectives

To compare clinical characteristics, tic phenomenology, severity, and treatment patterns in individuals with tic disorders with and without comorbid ASD.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 535 participants from Calgary Child and Adult Tic Disorders Clinical Registries. Tic severity was assessed using the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale (YGTSS). Comorbidities, tic phenomenology, and pharmacological treatments were recorded. ASD and non-ASD groups were compared using t-tests and chi-square tests.

Results

Mean age at tic onset was 6.79 years; 73.3% were male, and 9.2% had ASD. ASD was associated with higher rates of complex motor (arm 20.4% vs 9.9%; hand 24.5% vs 13.9%) and vocal tics (phrases 12.2% vs 3.5%; palilalia 20.4% vs 8.3%; blocking/stuttering 16.3% vs 6.2%) compared with non-ASD participants (all P < 0.05), with similar overall severity. ASD was also associated with higher rates of ADHD (81.6% vs 44.7%) and greater use of guanfacine, aripiprazole, risperidone, methylphenidate, and dextroamphetamine compared with non-ASD participants (all P < 0.05). In multivariable analysis, ASD was independently associated with lower tic-related impairment (β = -4.49, 95% CI -8.46 to -0.51; P = 0.027).

Conclusions

Comorbid ASD in tic disorders is associated with higher rates of complex motor and vocal tics, while severity is similar to non-ASD. Lower tic-related impairment may reflect communication differences. Comorbid symptoms influenced treatment supporting the need for individualized management.

raw.abstractText: Desiderosmia, the compulsive craving to smell non-food odours, is an under-recognised manifestation of iron deficiency anaemia (IDA). We report a 15-year-old boy with a one-year history of compulsive inhalation of petrol and kerosene along with mild fatigue on exertion. Investigations confirmed severe IDA (haemoglobin 5.8 g/dL) with elevated inflammatory markers and positive faecal lactoferrin. Sigmoidoscopy demonstrated Mayo grade 2 ulcerative colitis. raw.abstractText: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a significant public health concern globally. Among the most prevalent NCDs the study aims to explore the association of some elements with the the likelihood of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) development. In this cross-sectional case control study, 300 individuals with CVDs (n = 110), T2D (n = 70), and a control group (n = 120) from the Ravansar Non-Communicable Disease (RaNCD) cohort in western Iran were examined. The RaNCD cohort is part of the PERSIAN cohort study, consisting of 10,000 adults. Participants aged 35-65 were stratified into three clusters based on their health status. Various elements, including aluminum (Al), calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), phosphorus (P), manganese (Mn), potassium (K), cobalt (Co), lithium (Li), boron (B), molybdenum (Mo), and vanadium (V) in the blood serum was performed using the ICP-MS method, and data were analyzed using multivariable techniques, including logistic regression and clustering analysis. Our analysis revealed a notable association between most elements and the risks of CVD and T2D in the logistic regression model after adjusting for age and gender. Specifically, increased odds ratios of CVD and T2D were identified for higher Ca, Mn, Mg, Li, V, Al, P, and Mo levels. In the T2D group, four clusters were identified: Al-B, Mn-Co-Mo, K-P, and V-Li-Ca-Mg. In the CVD group, five clusters were observed: K, B-Co-Mo, Li-Mg, Ca-P, and Mn-Al-V. The study provides valuable insights into the role of some essential elements in the development of CVDs and T2D. The key elements that are most linked to the elevated risk of CVDs and T2D include calcium, manganese, molybdenum, vanadium, lithium, aluminum, phosphorus, and magnesium. Further exploration of the intricate relationships between elements and disease risk could enhance our understanding of preventive strategies and personalized interventions for individuals at risk of CVDs and T2D.

raw.abstractText: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is associated with a hypoxic microenvironment that stabilizes hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α), driving glycolytic flux and lactate accumulation. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death process linked to lactate metabolism, has been implicated in UC pathogenesis; however, whether HIF-1α regulates ferroptosis through protein lactylation remains unclear. Bioinformatic analysis identified HIF-1α as a pivotal node connecting lactylation and ferroptosis signatures, with the lactylation score showing a strong positive correlation with ferroptosis activity, suggesting its upstream regulatory role. In cellular UC models, both protein lactylation and ferroptosis markers were significantly elevated. Inhibition of lactate synthesis reduced intracellular Fe<sup>2+</sup> overload and normalized expression of ferroptosis-related proteins. Mechanistically, knockdown of HIF-1α in colonic epithelial cells downregulated key glycolytic enzymes, including HK2, decreased lactate production and subsequent protein lactylation, and ultimately attenuated lipid peroxidation and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, thereby suppressing ferroptosis. Conversely, HIF-1α overexpression promoted ferroptosis-associated alterations in a glycolysis-dependent manner, and exogenous lactate partially restored these alterations upon HIF-1α silencing, supporting a HIF-1α-lactate-lactylation-ferroptosis cascade. We further screened for pharmacological inhibitors of HIF-1α and identified quercetin as a candidate through molecular docking and binding kinetics. Functional validation in vitro and in vivo demonstrated that quercetin directly binds and inhibits HIF-1α, thereby blocking the lactylation-ferroptosis axis and ameliorating colitis. Collectively, this study elucidates a novel HIF-1α-lactylation-ferroptosis regulatory axis in UC and proposes quercetin as a potential therapeutic agent that targets this "metabolism-cell death" network.

raw.abstractText: Isoniazid (INH) is a cornerstone antimicrobial for tuberculosis treatment, yet its potential immunomodulatory interactions with host innate immune effectors remain poorly characterized. Myeloperoxidase (MPO), an abundant neutrophil heme peroxidase involved in pathogen clearance, oxidizes INH into radical intermediates. This study investigated the biochemical and immunopharmacological effects of INH on MPO-dependent oxidative bacterial killing using Mycobacterium smegmatis mc<sup>2</sup>155 as a model. Using competitive kinetics with taurine, we demonstrated that INH reacts rapidly with hypochlorous acid (HOCl), with a second-order rate constant of 3.7 x 10<sup>7</sup> M<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>. This reaction markedly impaired HOCl-mediated bactericidal activity, while INH retained most of its antimicrobial activity. In purified enzymatic assays, INH significantly reduced MPO/H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>-mediated bacterial killing, restoring bacterial survival by up to approximately 70%. Furthermore, in human neutrophil-mediated killing assays, INH increased mycobacterial survival, with effects comparable to those observed with inhibitors of MPO and NADPH oxidase. INH did not significantly inhibit superoxide (O<sub>2</sub>•<sup>-</sup>) generation by activated neutrophils, indicating that its effects occur downstream of the primary NADPH oxidase-mediated oxidative burst. Together, these findings demonstrate that INH interferes with the MPO/HOCl antimicrobial pathway through both MPO inhibition and HOCl scavenging, revealing a previously underrecognized interaction between this first-line antimycobacterial drug and neutrophil oxidative antimicrobial mechanisms.

payload.abstract: Vitamin D is a nutrient and prohormone obtained from diet and supplements and synthesized in the skin. It is essential for calcium and phosphate homeostasis and skeletal health and influences multiple extra-skeletal processes, yet deficiency remains common worldwide. This narrative review summarizes vitamin D sources, physiology, metabolism, pharmacokinetics, clinical relevance and safety and outlines the distinct pharmacokinetic profiles and clinical roles of vitamin D, calcidiol and calcitriol and its analogues. Evidence consistently supports vitamin D, combined with calcium, for preventing and treating deficiency-related skeletal disorders in high-risk populations, and in specific conditions such as malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism and frailty. In vitamin D-replete populations, large trials show limited extra-skeletal benefits, apart from modest effects on cancer mortality and progression from prediabetes to Type 2 diabetes. Untargeted screening is not recommended. Future research should prioritize targeted supplementation, standardized assays and identification of populations most likely to benefit from supplementation.

payload.title: Ascorbate is a physiological tumor suppressor metabolite in leukemia
payload.abstract: Accumulation of oncometabolites promotes tumorigenesis, but it is not known if there are naturally occurring tumor suppressor metabolites whose deficiency within cancer-initiating cells causes cancer. Hematopoietic-specific ascorbate depletion promoted leukemogenesis by acting within leukemia initiating cells. Ascorbate depletion in myeloid leukemia expanded plasmacytoid dendritic cells, an effect mediated by the ascorbate molecular targets TET2 and TET3. Leukemia cells accumulated ascorbate as part of a tumor suppressor response to neoplastic proliferation that limited progression but depleted circulating ascorbate. Ascorbate restoration in mice with established leukemias extended survival. Hematopoietic-specific ascorbate depletion caused leukemia in collaboration with TET2 loss and was sufficient to cause leukemia with high penetrance even in the absence of other engineered mutations. These results identify ascorbate as a physiological tumor suppressor metabolite in blood cancers.

proposals.rationale: This study provides human observational evidence relevant to serum magnesium and cardiometabolic disease risk.
evidenceQuotes: In this cross-sectional case control study, 300 individuals with CVDs (n = 110), T2D (n = 70), and a control group (n = 120) from the Ravansar Non-Communicable Disease (RaNCD) cohort in western Iran were examined.

Various elements, including aluminum (Al), calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), phosphorus (P), manganese (Mn), potassium (K), cobalt (Co), lithium (Li), boron (B), molybdenum (Mo), and vanadium (V) in the blood serum was performed using the ICP-MS method

payload.population: Kurdish adults aged 35-65 in western Iran

proposals.rationale: The abstract reports serum magnesium in relation to both cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus risk.
evidenceQuotes: Specifically, increased odds ratios of CVD and T2D were identified for higher Ca, Mn, Mg, Li, V, Al, P, and Mo levels.

payload.effect: Higher serum magnesium levels were associated with increased odds of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus after adjustment for age and gender.

proposals.rationale: The study directly reports increased odds of both outcomes for higher serum magnesium levels, but does not establish causation.
evidenceQuotes: Our analysis revealed a notable association between most elements and the risks of CVD and T2D in the logistic regression model after adjusting for age and gender.
Specifically, increased odds ratios of CVD and T2D were identified for higher Ca, Mn, Mg, Li, V, Al, P, and Mo levels.

payload.caution: The findings are observational associations from a cross-sectional case-control study and should not be interpreted as evidence that higher magnesium causes cardiovascular disease or type 2 diabetes mellitus.

proposals.rationale: The design and abstract wording support an association but do not establish temporality or causality.

payload.claim: Quercetin is proposed as a potential therapeutic agent targeting the HIF-1α-lactylation-ferroptosis network in ulcerative colitis.

evidenceQuotes: Collectively, this study elucidates a novel HIF-1α-lactylation-ferroptosis regulatory axis in UC and proposes quercetin as a potential therapeutic agent that targets this "metabolism-cell death" network.
